Subject: Redwood Dedicated capacity expansion ETA (us-west / H100)

Following up on our expansion request for +16x H100 in us-west on our existing Dedicated pool (ACME-PROD-03). We’re planning a feature launch the week of Feb 17 and need to confirm when the additional capacity will be available for routing.

Can you share an ETA and if there’s any expected disruption during the add?

Platform Engineering

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@acmefintech.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated capacity expansion ETA (us-west / H100)

Hi Avery,

Yes — we can support +16x H100 in us-west for ACME-PROD-03.

Current ETA: we expect the new nodes to be marked Ready and eligible for routing by end of day Thu Feb 13 (PT), assuming no cloud quota friction. In practice we’re targeting a 60–120 min controlled window where we do the actual attach + validation.

Re: disruption: we keep the new capacity OUT of routing until it passes readiness gates (so there shouldn’t be impact to existing traffic). The only customer-visible change is once the pool scales up, you may see improved headroom / lower queueing.

Proposed maintenance window (PT): Thu Feb 13, 1:00–3:00 AM.

What “readiness gates” means on our side:
- Provisioning: infra alloc + network policy checks
- Imaging: golden image + pinned drivers/runtime prereqs
- Bootstrapping: k8s/node agents + runtime chart install
- Validating: GPU health checks (ECC/thermals), DNS/TLS, internal connectivity
- Perf canary: lightweight benchmark to verify throughput/latency within expected bounds

We’ll only mark the pool Ready (and expose to routing) after all gates pass.

If the proposed window works for you, reply “approved” and confirm if you want us to post updates in this thread or loop in a broader distro.

Thanks,
Vanessa

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Engineering Manager, Fleet Automation
Redwood Inference

Thanks — can we shift the window to Fri Feb 14 (00:00–02:00 AM PT) instead? Thursday night we have an internal deployment.

Also, can you confirm the expansion doesn’t “partially” route (e.g., a subset of nodes comes online before validation is complete)? We’ve been burned by that with other vendors.

Avery



From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@acmefintech.com>
Cc: IT Ops Oncall <it-ops-oncall@acmefintech.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 9:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated capacity expansion ETA (us-west / H100)

Hi Avery,

Fri Feb 14 00:00–02:00 AM PT works on our side — confirmed.

On partial routing: we do NOT route to the new nodes until they’re fully Ready. Concretely:
- The pool’s existing capacity remains in service.
- New nodes enter a Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating state.
- Only after the perf-canary completes successfully do we flip the control plane “Ready” flag for that capacity slice, at which point routing can advertise it.

If anything fails during validation (GPU health, networking, TLS, or perf-canary thresholds), we keep the new nodes out of rotation and either remediate (replace the bad node, re-run validation) or roll back the add. Existing capacity continues to serve traffic normally.

Attached is a short one-pager that outlines the gates and what we check. (It’s the same flow we’ll use for this expansion.)

Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Readiness_Gates_OnePager.pdf

Day-of plan:
- 00:00 PT: start window, begin provisioning run
- We’ll post stage updates here (and we can also ping the IT Ops Oncall address you included)
- Target Ready: ~01:00–01:30 PT
- 02:00 PT: hard stop; if not Ready by then we’ll keep new capacity out of routing and schedule follow-up

If you reply “approved” to proceed with Fri’s window, we’ll lock it in.

Thanks,
Vanessa

—
